audit.method: every entry traced to a file, table or endpoint verified to exist in the repository or live database
audit.headline_finding: A purpose classifier already exists inside Agent 2 (ROPA): app/agents/ropa/rules/purpose_rules.py (136 lines, 10 business purposes), app/agents/ropa/services/purpose_service.py (80 lines), app/agents/ropa/services/processing_activity_service.py (127 lines), plus a purpose_taxonomy table with 4 rows. Agent 1 independently classifies purpose as trackers.category / cookies.category, whose values were verified to be a strict subset of purpose_taxonomy.code. The missing capability is comparison, not classification.

missing_components.detail: No access logs, query logs, export logs, column lineage, ETL metadata or event tracking exist in code or schema. Purpose is inferred from table NAMES only via match_table(table_name). The only observed-usage signal in the platform is Agent 1's consent_states.

missing_components.component: declared vs observed comparison for purpose
missing_components.detail: The pattern exists for schema (ropa_schema_baselines vs ropa_schema_changes) but nothing compares declared purpose to observed purpose.
ROPA's 10 business purposes and Agent 1's 4 taxonomy codes are different vocabularies at different granularities. Nothing maps between them.
dsr_retention_rules and cookies.expiry exist but are never compared to a purpose.
policies stores url and policy_type only. extracted_text_ref is present on the record but excluded from prompts and dereferenced by nothing.
New migration required, including RLS enable/force/policy/grant and any enumerated CHECKs.

known_traps: Enumerated CHECK constraints are invisible to Python. Migrations 0021, 0023 and 0024 exist solely to widen one. Guards: tests/test_job_types_match_schema.py, test_status_values_match_schema.py, test_stage_names_match_schema.py.
New tables must opt into RLS explicitly - migration 0018 forced it on existing tables only. See migrations/0022 for the enable/force/policy/grant pattern.

Background jobs bind no org scope and work only because the worker connects as the database owner. Any path that might run as consiva_app must call apply_org_scope (see app/services/webhook_service.py:_save).

edges.rationale: Read trackers, cookies, consent_signals. Agent 1 must not import purpose code; its evidence tables are already the contract.
purpose_service and processing_activity_service are pure functions over DiscoveryEvidence. Reuse without duplicating.
Read declared purpose from ropa_records.payload. Do not write it.

edges.mechanism: MUST NOT BE A DIRECT DEPENDENCY
edges.rationale: Writing purpose back into ropa_records creates ROPA -> purpose -> ROPA. ROPA's next run would overwrite it and the two would disagree silently.
Already how every agent is triggered. No new mechanism.

dependency_map.circular_dependency_risk: Real. ROPA already computes purpose. The classifier must READ declared purpose and WRITE assessments to its own tables.

purpose_classifier_requirements.recommendation: Build a reconciliation service, not a sixth agent-shaped classifier.
rationale: Purpose classification already exists twice: purpose_rules.py (10 business purposes, table-name driven) and trackers/cookies.category (4 taxonomy codes, vendor-signature driven). A third classifier produces three disagreeing answers.
Nine of thirteen steps in the required conceptual flow already exist. The missing capability is comparison, not classification.
The declared-vs-observed pattern is already implemented for schema in ropa_schema_baselines vs ropa_schema_changes.

The highest-value finding needs no new ingestion: a tracker categorised 'marketing' whose consent_states include 'pre_consent' is observed processing without a lawful basis. Both halves are already in the database and nothing joins them.

proposed_modules.purpose: map ROPA's 10 business purposes to purpose_taxonomy's 4 codes

purpose_classifier_requirements.accuracy_constraint: purpose_rules.py returns None rather than guessing and the caller emits 'Unknown' with review_required=True. Any new comparison must inherit that discipline. This codebase has a documented false-positive incident (tests/test_consent_banner_false_positive.py) where keyword matching against a user's forum comment produced a high-priority finding about a consent banner that did not exist. A declared-vs-observed mismatch reported confidently, when the real cause is a vocabulary-mapping artefact, is worse than no finding.
